# tree-sitter-ocaml (vendored by sloplint)

## Origin

- Published crate: `tree-sitter-ocaml` 0.26.0 (crates.io). Name and version are unchanged.
- Upstream: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-ocaml.
- License: MIT (`LICENSE` is the upstream file, fetched verbatim).
- Files kept from the crate: `Cargo.toml` (normalized by cargo), `LICENSE`, `bindings/`, `common/`, `grammars/` (grammar.js patched), `queries/`, `tree-sitter.json`.
- `Cargo.toml` has one addition: an empty `[workspace]` table after `[lib]`. Without it `cargo fmt --all` reports the vendored package as belonging to the parent workspace and fails. No other manifest change.
- `common/scanner.h` is patched (external cppo/opa directive tokens, shared `#`-dispatch with `line_number_directive`; see change 6). The per-grammar `grammars/*/src/scanner.c` shims are upstream files and need no edits — the shared header carries the scan logic.
- Files dropped: `Cargo.toml.orig`, `Cargo.lock`, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, `.cargo-ok`.
- The crate ships three grammars — `grammars/ocaml` (scope `source.ocaml`, `.ml`), `grammars/interface` (`source.ocaml.interface`, `.mli`), and `grammars/type` (`source.ocaml.type`). `interface` and `type` `import` the ocaml `grammar.js`, so all grammar edits live in `grammars/ocaml/grammar.js` and all three `src/` trees must be regenerated together.
- `ocaml.so` at the crate root is the compiled `grammars/ocaml` parser (built with `tree-sitter build`); it exists for external tool dogfooding only — the Rust crate compiles all three parsers statically via `bindings/rust/build.rs`.

## Why

The published grammar reports a parse error on valid OCaml written for camlp5-style preprocessors; a parse error can hide most of a file's lint findings. The largest corpus cluster is HOL Light (camlp5 quotations everywhere): against the corpus the published grammar errors on ~881 of 980 `.ml` files in github-hol-light; the patched grammar errors on ~831 files by raw `tree-sitter parse` (825 files carry `meta/parse-error` findings under `sloplint check`) — the residual is documented below.

## Regeneration

`src/` is regenerated with tree-sitter-cli 0.27.x (`tree-sitter-0.27.1 generate`); the grammar uses `reserved`, which CLI 0.24 cannot emit. Run `generate` inside each of `grammars/ocaml`, `grammars/interface`, and `grammars/type`. The patched inputs are `grammars/ocaml/grammar.js` and `common/scanner.h`; `src/grammar.json`, `src/node-types.json`, and `src/parser.c` are regenerated artifacts and are not part of `sloplint-grammar.patch`. The patch applies to a pristine crate checkout with `patch -p0` run from the crate root (the `+++` paths are crate-root-relative: `grammars/ocaml/grammar.js`, `common/scanner.h`).

## Changes (`grammars/ocaml/grammar.js`, see `sloplint-grammar.patch`)

Each change is an OCaml construct the published grammar rejects.

1. **camlp5 tagged quotations.** `<:expr< ... >>`, `<:patt< ... >>`, `<:ctyp< ... >>`, `<:str_item< ... >>`, `<:sig_item< ... >>`, `<:class_expr< ... >>`, `<:vala< ... >>`, `<:module_expr< ... >>`, `<:module_type< ... >>`, `<:class_str_item< ... >>` — any `<:ident< ... >>` parses as an opaque `quotation` node with nested quotations allowed. `quotation` is an alternative wherever a camlp5 quote can appear: `_structure_item`, `_signature_item`, `_module_type`, `_type`, `_simple_expression`, `_simple_pattern`.
2. **Backtick term quotations.** `` `?n. n + 0 = n` ``-style quotes parse as an opaque `term_quotation` token — but only when the first character cannot start an identifier or raw identifier. `` `foo `` is lexically identical to a polymorphic-variant tag (`match x with `A -> 1`), so quotes that open with a letter (Unicode included, since the grammar's identifiers are Unicode-aware), `_`, `'`, or `\` (raw-identifier tags like `` `\#let ``) are deliberately not covered; digits and punctuation do open a quotation.
3. **Quotation as a binding pattern.** `let <:patt< `A >> = f 1` — `_simple_binding_pattern` admits `quotation`/`term_quotation`, matching `_simple_pattern`.
4. **Tag charset widened** to `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9.:]*` — location-binding tags (`<:expr:<`), module-qualified tags (`<:m.n<`), and registered custom expanders (`<:xhtml<`, `<:sexp_of<`, `<:reloc_expr<` all occur in the corpus).
5. **Declared conflicts** for the ambiguity the quotation alternatives introduce: `[$._structure_item, $._simple_expression]`, `[$.let_binding]`, `[$.class_binding]`, `[$.application_expression]`, `[$._signature_item, $._type]`, `[$._class_expression, $.class_application]`, `[$.class_application]`, `[$._camlp4_any_directive, $.camlp4_conditional]`, `[$._match_cases]`.
6. **cppo directives** (`#define`, `#include`, `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#endif`, `#else`, `#elif`, `#undef`, `#error`, `#warning`, `#pragma`, `#line`, `#ext`, `#endext`, `#stop`, `#localization`). `cppo_directive`, `cppo_directive_no_arrow`, and `opa_directive` are **external tokens** scanned in `common/scanner.h` (shared by all three grammars via each `grammars/*/src/scanner.c` shim). A `#` only dispatches to the directive scanners when it starts a line or follows whitespace (`skipped_ws || column == 0`); a `#` butted against the previous token (`obj#error x`, `obj##name`) stays a `#`/`##` method call or hash operator — mid-expression method calls like `log#error (fun y -> y)` (aeneas, links, setml, ocaml-caqti) parse exactly as upstream. The scanner shares one `#` consumption with the pre-existing `# N "file"` `line_number_directive` path (which still requires strict column 0). Once claimed, the scanner swallows the whole directive line, including `\`-newline continuations (`#define FOO a \ <newline> b c`). Inside the `#` block the scanner picks a candidate by the first character after `#`: `##` dispatches to `opa_directive` (whose name must be ASCII — `succ ##été` stays a `##` hash expression), a digit/space/tab at column 0 dispatches to `line_number_directive`, and anything else tries the cppo name table — a failed name match (`#get#value`, `#log2 "x"`) returns false instead of falling through to the opa or line-marker paths. The directive name is prefix-matched (`#ifdefx` claims `if` + tail `defx`, mirroring the old regex alternation). Accepted casualty: `o #error x` — a method call written with a space before `#` — claims a directive; that spacing does not occur in the corpus. Valid at structure/signature level and inside `_match_cases`, where directives may appear before `|`, between `|` and its arm (`| #ifdef Y` mid-line), and after the last arm (`#ifdef STRINGLIT | `Stringlit _ -> ... #endif` in yojson's `util.ml`). Inside expressions `#` remains the method-call operator (`obj #m`), so cppo directives are deliberately not expression-level. In `_match_cases` the slots use `cppo_directive_no_arrow` (aliased to `cppo_directive`): an arm may start with a polymorphic-variant type pattern (`| #error as e -> pp`, mirage-tcpip/ocaml-git/httpaf/vpnkit/ocaml-tls), so the token requires a `->`-free line to be all-or-nothing — `| #error ... -> body` fails the token and parses as a pattern arm. Arrow detection skips `"..."` arguments so `#warning "a -> b"` still reads as a directive, `'x'` char literals are skipped so `#define RPAREN ')'` keeps its delimiters — a `'` after an identifier char is a name apostrophe instead (`ADD'(x)`, `e'->`), and a `)` that would close an enclosing pair ends the token so a directive inside parentheses (`o #define (fun y -> y))`) keeps the parens balanced. Only a `->` at paren depth 0 separates an arm pattern from its body, so `#define when (fun x -> x)` reads as a directive, not a guarded arm — unless a `->` starts the next line, which marks a multi-line arm (`| #name when g\n -> e`, `| #error\n -> e`, peeked without consuming past the newline). The peek is skipped when the tail can't be an arm prefix: conditional-section names (`#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#elif`, `#else`, `#endif` and prefix-matches) with a bare or literal-only tail are always directives — a bare `#endif` or quoted `#include "x"` never claims an enclosing arm's arrow — while `when`/`as` tails stay arm-shaped for every name, including section names used as variant tags (`| #ifdef as e`) — except `when =`/`as =`, which are cppo conditions over macros named `when`/`as`. Literals after a same-line `->` are body text and never disqualify the arm (`| #error -> "boom"`). An arrow-bearing line whose pre-`->` text is ` as <ident>`, optionally followed by a `when` guard, or `when <expr>`, or empty — the shapes of `| `#name as v [when g] -> ...` and `| `#name when g ->` polymorphic-variant arms — refuses for *every* name (`#error`, `#warning`, `#stop`, `#defined`, ...), while any other arrow-bearing line emits `cppo_directive_no_arrow` so a `#define g (fun x -> x)` between arms stays preprocessing text and the match stays open; `cppo_directive` covers the structure-level-only case. Strings inside a tail may span newlines — scanning continues to the closing quote, so a `->` at line-start inside a literal (`| #error when "a\n -> b"`) is content, not an arm separator, while `when "a\nb" = x -> e` still reads as a guarded arm. `{|...|}`/`{delim|...|delim}` raw strings inside a tail are skipped whole, so a `"` inside one is content, not a string opener. `cppo_directive_no_arrow` no longer consumes the trailing newline into the token, keeping its text identical to the structure-level `cppo_directive`. A `|`-prefixed directive line folds its `|` into the directive, so the next `|` still separates the following case (`| `A -> 1 | #endif | `B -> 2`).
7. **camlp4 directives and conditional sections.** `#<Name>` / `#<Name:args>` / `#<Name args>` (`#<If:TESTING>`, `#<Else>`, `#<Ifstatic:OCAML_VERSION_MAJOR 4>`, `#<If$minlevel 10>`) parse as an opaque `camlp4_directive` token; `#<End>` is a dedicated higher-precedence `camlp4_end_directive` token so a conditional unambiguously terminates. A `#<X> expr #<Y> expr #<End>` run reduces to `camlp4_conditional`, which is an expression (`let to_string = #<If:TESTING> a #<Else> function | ... #<End>` in opalang's `ident.ml`). Arm expressions are required — a `#<If>` arm whose body is itself a conditional parses unambiguously nested (`#<If:A> #<If:B> x #<End> #<Else> y #<End>`). Bare directives also stand alone at structure/signature level. `_match_cases` accepts only `cppo_directive` separators: a `#<Else>` shifted into the case list would steal the arm separator of an enclosing conditional.
8. **opa/qml bypass forms.** `##name args` bypass directives and `#<< ... >>#;` bypass quotations (opalang) parse as `opa_directive` / `opa_quotation` tokens; `opa_quotation` is also a `_simple_expression` and a `_parameter`, where opa splices instrumentation (`let plot #<< debugid >># prefix = ...`). `opa_directive` is an external token gated on the same whitespace/line-start rule as cppo — `obj##name` stays a `##` method call — and requires an identifier char after `##` so Js_of_ocaml-style `##.` can never lex as a directive.

## Known remaining gaps

- **Bare `<<...>>` quotations are not supported.** `<<` is a legal custom infix operator in real OCaml (bap defines `let (<<) p q = ...` and uses `p << q`), so a `<<` quotation opener regresses valid operator code. ~40 hol-light files use bare `<<`.
- **Identifier-opening backtick quotes** (`` `foo ...` ``) are textually identical to polymorphic-variant tags; longest-match token stealing regresses every `match` arm in standard OCaml (measured: bap 0→240). Documented camlp5 ceiling — these need real preprocessing.
- **`expr <:tag< expr` infix chains** (`a <:x< b`) collide with the quotation opener when a `>>` follows later — custom `<:`-prefixed operators are a documented ceiling (zero occurrences in the ~4,200-repo corpus; bap-style `<<`/`>>` ops are unaffected).
- **Directives inside application argument lists** (`f #<Ifstatic:X> ~labeled:arg #<End> arg`) — letting directives into `_argument` mis-resolves `#<End>` arms and regresses conditionals (measured: opalang objectFiles.ml 0→150 errors); needs real preprocessing to know which arm survives.
- **opa splices in arbitrary keyword positions** (`module M (P : T) #<< (X : T) >># = struct` — a quotation between the functor parameter list and `=`); 2 residual errors in opalang's debugTracer.ml/.mli.
- **camlp4 `parser`/`lexer` stream syntax** (`let aux = parser | [< e = p; s >] -> ... | [< >] -> ...`) — a separate stream-pattern grammar; ~3 opalang files (jsParse, indexer).
- **camlp4 markers inside sequence/list elements** (`[ "a"; #<Ifstatic> "b"; #<End> "c" ]` and `Printf f; #<End> let x = ... in`) — `#<End>` as a mid-sequence separator conflicts with its role as conditional terminator; ~3 opalang files (qml2ocamlOptions, qmlCpsServerLib).
- hol-light residual: ~831/980 `.ml` files by raw parse, almost all ident-opening term quotations and bare `<<`.
- Spot checks after the external-directive round (files carrying `meta/parse-error` findings, corpus `repos_big`): opalang 22 (was 89 — zero new-only errors, 67 fixed; residuals are `parser`/sequence-element `#<...>` ceilings and functor-parameter `#<< >>#` splices), batteries-included 29 (mostly `[? ... ?]` comprehension), ocamlformat 43 (mostly `test/failing/` intentionally-broken fixtures), lwt 2, bap 2, yojson 1, aeneas/links/ocaml-caqti 0.
